title.purpose: Group labels and nav-scale UI type.

script.purpose: Condiment accent overlapping a heading, Signal Lime, mix-blend exclusion, tilted -1 to -2deg.

body.purpose: Uppercase mono paragraphs and metadata rows.

label.purpose: Tags, counts, fine print; widest tracking.

shadows.name: violet-glow

shadows.name: glass-edge
shadows.purpose: Part of the liquid-glass recipe; an edge highlight, not a depth cue.

components.name: Bar Button
components.description: The primary action shape: an Anton uppercase word over a 6px Signal Lime bar that shrinks on hover. No box, no background.

components.name: Bar Button (Alt)
components.description: Secondary action beside a neon one; identical shape, the bar carries the violet gradient.

components.name: Go Button
components.description: 48px violet-gradient circle with a cream chevron; carries the system's only glow shadow. Opens a card.

components.name: Navigation Pill
components.description: Liquid-glass pill of Anton uppercase links; hover and active answer in Signal Lime.

components.name: Tag
components.description: Liquid-glass keyword pill on modal metadata; uppercase mono.

components.name: Copy Toast
components.description: The copy-feedback pill: Signal Lime on Abyss Navy, fixed bottom-center in the app, rises 10px with its fade.

narrative.overview: A shelf drifting in deep space. Every screen you ever saved is cargo in a dark hold: nebula gradients and twinkling stars behind, noise texture over everything, mono telemetry labels naming each item. The surface is a personal tool, but it presents itself like an NFT landing page (the reference system is Orbis.Nft), because in this app the collection IS the show. The component doctrine is loud type, quiet chrome. Anton does the shouting in full uppercase; containers are barely-there liquid glass; buttons are words with a neon bar under them, not boxes. Motion follows the same split: one orchestrated hero entrance, quiet scroll reveals everywhere else, and 200ms exits.
keyCharacteristics: Deep-navy space scene (nebula + stars + noise) behind every major section
All type uppercase except the cursive accent; mono for everything that isn't a heading
Liquid glass as the only container treatment; no opaque panels
One neon accent doing all interactive feedback; violet reserved for the circular go button
Sections capped at 1831px; section corners 32px, media 24px
One entrance choreography, then restraint: reveals ≤650ms, state changes ≤300ms

rules.name: The Closed Palette Rule
rules.body: Five tokens, no additions. Need a gray? Use Starlight Cream at reduced opacity. Need emphasis? Use scale or the accent, never a new hue.

rules.name: The Gradient Cage Rule
rules.body: The violets exist only as the 135deg pair on the go button (and the alt bar). A flat violet fill anywhere is a violation.

rules.name: The Case Rule
rules.body: Everything is uppercase except Condiment, which is never uppercase.

rules.name: The Overlap Rule
rules.body: Condiment never sits in its own row. It overlaps a heading's corner, slightly rotated, or it doesn't appear.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The go button's violet glow is the only blur shadow in the system. Any other box-shadow with blur is forbidden.

dos: Do keep every section inside the 1831px max-width wrap, sections at 32px radius, media at 24px.
Do make new interactive elements answer in Signal Lime (#6FFF00): bar, glow, or text shift; nothing else signals interactivity.
Do derive every gray from Starlight Cream opacity steps (.8 / .7 / .6 / .45).
Do animate with transform and opacity only, easing on --ease-out / --ease-out-expo, and keep exits at ~75% of enter durations.
Do reuse BarButton / GoButton from src/ui.jsx instead of restyling <button>.
donts: Don't use emoji in the UI.
Don't introduce colors outside the five tokens; no new grays, no flat violet fills.
Don't add blur shadows anywhere except the go button's violet glow.
Don't set normal-case type in anything but Condiment.
Don't give buttons backgrounds, borders, or boxes; a bar button is a word and a bar.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, margins) or ship motion that ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't add a second orchestrated entrance; the hero owns page-load choreography, everything else reveals quietly on scroll.
